artifacts.qualification: Module compiled and validated locally; publication and real AIO registry resolution/deployment must be verified separately.

configuration.format: A complete JSON object; graph defaults supply role, the predictor demo bootstrap, and full factory inputTopics for the five reading roles (including the running-total sensor-1 bootstrap). Overrides replace the entire object.

configuration.value: <complete JSON settings object encoded as a string>

configuration.limits: Counts must be positive: maxAssets <=1024, other counts <=4096. Non-lateness durations in 1..86400000 ms; allowedLatenessMs in 0..60000 and less than pendingTtlMs. Counts bound records, not a fixed memory budget; size limits and payload size must be chosen for runtime memory.
configuration.validation: Unknown configuration fields, duplicate bootstrap assets, non-finite coefficients and version 0 bootstrap are rejected. Identifiers are 1..128 bytes without control characters; input JSON objects are at most 65536 bytes. Configurations are immutable for one operator initialization.

alignment.timestamp: RFC3339 with timezone, Unix epoch or later, precision milliseconds or coarser. Future event timestamps more than maxFutureSkewMs ahead of the processing clock are errors. Historical replay is allowed.
alignment.selection: For each asset choose newest temperature at or before the speed timestamp, with age <=maxContextAgeMs. Never use future context. Temperatures at or behind an already established watermark are tooLate; speeds strictly behind it are tooLate.
alignment.readiness: Per-asset watermark = maximum accepted event/tick sampledAt minus allowedLatenessMs. A speed finalizes when watermark >= its sampledAt OR processing elapsed since buffering >=allowedLatenessMs, evaluated only on input arrivals. A tick sampledAt >=speed sampledAt+allowedLatenessMs flushes an event-time tail immediately; alternatively send a tick after the processing-time wait. No background timer exists.
alignment.idleTail: Publish a trusted periodic tick for each active asset on a subscribed speed topic. Quiescent graphs cannot emit, expire, or count diagnostics until another input arrives. For recorded fixtures publish the final tick, not just the three original docs messages.
alignment.output: One original speed record with kind removed plus temperature and temperatureSampledAt. No eligible context produces a noContext diagnostic, not a value. Several finalized records are delivered as {kind:batch,records:[...]}. Consumers must handle this envelope.
alignment.duplicates: Speed key is sampledAt + optional pieceId + optional runId within asset. Temperature key is sampledAt within asset. Identical retained payloads diagnose duplicate; differing payloads diagnose conflict and never replace the first. Same event instant with a differently formatted timestamp is a conflicting payload.
alignment.bounds: History is pruned below min(watermark,oldest pending timestamp)-maxContextAgeMs. History at capacity rejects new context, not evicts usable context; send advancing ticks. Completed-reading dedup capacity blocks finalization until capacity expires; a reading still blocked at pendingTtlMs emits expired. Assets with no pending/completed entries expire after pendingTtlMs of inactivity.

correlation.preservation: Original feature, coefficient, model and predictedAt/sampledAt fields from the prediction and all measured fields are retained. Optional sampledAt/predictedAt/measuredAt fields must be valid RFC3339 timestamps with at most millisecond precision. Shared non-key fields must be equal or the match fails explicitly; use predictedAt and measuredAt for different instants.
correlation.output: kind=correlated plus merged fields, residual=measuredWeight-predictedWeight, targetError=measuredWeight-targetWeight. Both arrival orders work.
correlation.retention: Pending TTL is processing-time age from first side, not refreshed by retries. Completed dedup TTL starts at completion. Identical duplicates are no-ops with diagnostics; conflicts never replace state. After completedTtlMs, replay can match again. Capacity rejects instead of evicting protected records. Any valid input or {kind:tick,assetId:...} cleans all assets and logs expiration diagnostics.

predictor.bootstrap: Graph default seeds line-1 v7 with speedCoefficient=2, temperatureCoefficient=0.5, intercept=175. No implicit model exists in the core: other assets get noActiveModel. Empty initialModels allows first update only with expectedModelVersion=0 and modelVersion=1.
predictor.activation: Model updates must come from an externally approved/authenticated source. Activate only expectedModelVersion == active version AND modelVersion == active version+1. An update is never an observation. Identical updateId payload diagnoses duplicateUpdate; differing reuse diagnoses conflictingUpdate. Old versions diagnose staleUpdate; gaps diagnose versionConflict. No state is changed on rejection.
predictor.output: Reading fields plus kind=prediction, active modelVersion, all three coefficients and predictedWeight=speed*speedCoefficient+temperature*temperatureCoefficient+intercept. Optional reading timestamps are preserved, never replaced by measurement-time values. Model fields supplied on readings must exactly agree with active model and calculated prediction.
predictor.bounds: Assets and accepted update payloads are bounded, never evicted. After maxUpdatesPerAsset, new updates reject with capacity until a coordinated bootstrap/restart. This avoids silently forgetting an updateId.

readingPatterns.inputTopicContract: SDK wrapper requires an exact complete typed JSON inputTopics object mapping kind to full MQTT topic for these five roles. Missing/extra/duplicate kind keys, non-string values, null, empty topics, wildcard/control characters and shared topics reject initialization. Topic matches are byte-exact, not suffix matches. Unknown/missing kinds or topic mismatches log/count errors and return SDK errors before core dispatch or any clock/state mutation. Native Engine permits absent bindings and has no MQTT authority. Original three roles are unchanged. Chart computes PREFIX from topicPrefix or dataflow-patterns/<release>; graph defaults and standalone manifests use factory. Authorize reading, tick, register and reset publishers separately at the broker; payload kind alone is not authorization.
readingPatterns.scope: The following five roles use the same Map component and separate suppress-internal Filter. These contracts do not change the original three roles. Each graph has one source and one sink; readings, trusted ticks and approved control inputs share the graph source. Input bindings must subscribe to every required topic.
readingPatterns.configuration: Only supply settings belonging to the selected role. Null numeric settings are invalid; omission selects the default. heartbeatIntervalMs omitted means disabled. deadband >0 finite; alpha in (0,1]; low < high, both finite. raiseForMs/clearForMs in 0..86400000; heartbeatIntervalMs/maxObservationGapMs/timeoutMs in 1..86400000. initialStates is only valid for running-total, even if empty. Unknown settings and bootstrap fields reject initialization.
readingPatterns.bounds: For these roles maxAssets defaults to and cannot exceed 128; assets never auto-expire or evict, and new assets at capacity reject. maxHistoryPerAsset defaults to 256, maximum 4096, and retains the most recent complete accepted reading payloads per asset, including suppressed readings. maxUpdatesPerAsset defaults to 512, maximum 4096, and independently retains the most recent accepted reset payloads per asset across epochs. All capacities must be positive. Each successful reading/reset evicts the oldest payload in its own full history, never blocking an advancing stream; rejected inputs and arithmetic errors never evict history. Retention is an accepted-record count lookback, not a time TTL. Numeric state, last observation and sequence/timestamp watermarks survive payload pruning; memory is O(maxAssets * (maxHistoryPerAsset + maxUpdatesPerAsset)) payloads plus per-asset state. A count bound is not a fixed memory budget: each input can be 65536 bytes. This is bounded retry/conflict detection, NOT durable exactly-once.

optional: sampledAt:RFC3339 timezone, epoch or later, precision milliseconds or coarser

readingPatterns.ordering: sequence must strictly increase within each asset, across resets too. The four non-total roles allow first sequence 0. Total bootstrap lastSequence is an already consumed watermark, so seed 0 requires first sequence >0. Producers must assign globally unique messageIds per asset (including across epochs), globally unique resetIds per asset, and retry only the identical payload with its original sequence/ID; sequence-derived IDs are recommended. Independent IDs are permitted under that uniqueness obligation. Equal retained messageId and complete JSON payload yields duplicate; differing reuse yields conflict. After eviction, original sequence <=watermark still yields staleReading and cannot double count. Reuse of an evicted ID with a NEWER sequence cannot be detected and can be accepted: enforcing producer uniqueness beyond the lookback requires an external durable log. Sequence <=watermark or regressing present sampledAt yields staleReading. Rejected inputs never refresh ages, reserve IDs, or replace state. Missing sampledAt does not erase the last present timestamp watermark. Equal sampledAt with advancing sequence is permitted. Deduplication is per asset and independent of sampledAt.
readingPatterns.time: Engine.process(input, nowMs) requires nondecreasing processing-clock epoch milliseconds. The SDK wrapper supplies SystemTime wall-clock time, which is not inherently monotonic; backward host-clock adjustments produce an explicit error, not a fabricated sample or clamped timestamp. Operators must keep the host clock synchronized and handle failed arrivals/retries. Optional sampledAt on every kind must be RFC3339 and no more than maxFutureSkewMs (default 30000) ahead of nowMs; it is preserved for provenance/ordering and NEVER advances a processing duration. Schema and arithmetic failures are explicit errors; temporal or asset-capacity rejections are diagnostic no-ops.

optional: sampledAt:validated but not used for durations
tick.semantics: One trusted arrival per asset, processed with the engine clock. Unknown ticks never allocate assets or emit offline. No autonomous timers, SDK sliding window, per-asset Window timeout, heartbeat publisher, or scheduler is implemented. Quiet graphs emit nothing without input; publish ticks often enough for required latency. Enforce trusted source authorization externally; payload kind is not authorization.

readingPatterns.preservation: Reading-derived records preserve all original JSON fields except kind, adding the documented output fields. Reserved output fields on any input are errors, not silently overwritten. Reset epoch is also reserved. Original messageId/sequence/sampledAt remain the observation identity on tick emissions. SDK transport metadata belongs to the triggering tick, so use JSON provenance, not transport timestamp, to identify measurements.

reportByException.decision: Emit first reading, then only when abs(value - LAST REPORTED value) >=deadband. Accepted suppressed readings update latest observation but not reported baseline. Boundary is inclusive. Identical duplicates never emit or refresh.
reportByException.output: Original reading with kind=reported, reason=initial|change|heartbeat, emittedAtMs, receivedAtMs, observationAgeMs=emittedAtMs-receivedAtMs, isFreshMeasurement.
reportByException.heartbeat: Optional trusted tick after elapsed >=heartbeatIntervalMs since last report emits latest accepted reading and moves the reported baseline to its value. Origin sampledAt/messageId/sequence remain unchanged; isFreshMeasurement=false, age continues growing until a NEW valid measurement arrives. Heartbeat is a report, not evidence that the sensor is online. Reading-triggered reports have isFreshMeasurement=true; suppressed readings alone do not trigger a heartbeat.

stableAlarm.decision: Startup normal, no initial cleared event. In normal state, value >=high starts/continues raise candidate; in active state, value <=low starts/continues clear candidate. A nonqualifying observation interrupts that candidate; hysteresis middle band leaves active state unchanged. Transition after candidate processing elapsed >=configured duration; zero means immediate. Outputs only on state changes.
stableAlarm.continuity: On every accepted reading or tick, a gap >maxObservationGapMs since last accepted observation resets pending duration, not active state. A new qualifying reading after a gap starts a new candidate. A tick can finish a candidate only while observationAgeMs <=maxObservationGapMs. This is an explicit observed-continuity policy, not proof of physical continuity between samples. Choose gap based on expected sampling cadence; ticks never count as observations.
stableAlarm.output: Original latest reading with kind=alarm, state=active|cleared, reason=thresholdSustained, threshold=high|low, emittedAtMs, receivedAtMs, observationAgeMs, isFreshMeasurement=false for tick or true for reading. Repeated active/normal readings and ticks do not spam transitions.

offlineDetection.registration: Optional register starts waiting for an expected asset at receipt processing time, allowing offline before the first measurement. Registration emits nothing and is idempotent without refreshing the watch. First reading also creates a watch. An unseen tick is never registration. The trusted allowlisted ticker publishes register on availability-registers each cycle before ticks, restoring the expected roster after graph restart without postponing an existing watch. Measurement identities must never have publish permission on availability-registers or availability-ticks.
offlineDetection.decision: Timeout age >=timeoutMs since last accepted measurement receipt (or initial registration if no measurement). Emit one offline transition per silence. Ticks are required to observe silence without readings. First valid reading emits online/firstReading, recovery emits online/recovered exactly once. A valid reading arriving after timeout with no intervening tick produces batch [offline, online recovered]. Duplicate/conflicting/stale/capacity-rejected measurements never refresh or recover.
offlineDetection.output: {kind:availability,assetId,state:online|offline,reason:firstReading|timeout|recovered,emittedAtMs,lastSeenAtMs,elapsedMs}. lastSeenAtMs is processing receipt time of last accepted measurement, null before any measurement. Offline elapsedMs is age since last measurement/registration; recovery elapsedMs is that age just before recovery, while firstReading elapsedMs=0.

runningTotal.bootstrap: Fail closed: readings and resets for assets absent from initialStates produce uninitializedAsset with no allocation. initialStates requires assetId, finite total, unsigned stateVersion/epoch/lastSequence, and optional lastSampledAt (last present accepted sampledAt watermark). Bootstrap assets count toward maxAssets. Do not use the zero demo bootstrap when recovering a nonzero checkpoint.
runningTotal.decision: Each accepted reading adds its signed value, increments stateVersion, and advances lastSequence. Its epoch must match active epoch or epochConflict. Duplicate IDs cannot double count while retained; stale sequences cannot reenter after reset/bootstrap. Finite sum and nonwrapping stateVersion are required atomically.
runningTotal.readingOutput: Original reading with kind=total, total, stateVersion, epoch, lastSequence=sequence, emittedAtMs; lastSampledAt is included if any accepted timestamp watermark exists, including when current reading omits sampledAt.
runningTotal.reset: Only explicitly approved reset source. expectedStateVersion must equal active version and reset sequence must exceed lastSequence. Success sets total=0, increments epoch AND stateVersion, advances lastSequence and retains sampledAt watermark and the bounded reading lookback. It appends to the independent reset lookback, evicting its oldest payload when full. Same retained resetId/full payload yields duplicateReset; changed reuse yields conflictReset. Evicted original reset retries still reject by expected version or sequence watermark. An evicted resetId reused with a new approved sequence AND current expectedStateVersion cannot be recognized as reuse: producers must enforce unique IDs externally. Version mismatch yields versionConflict; old sequence yields staleReading. Epoch/version overflow is an atomic error and does not prune history. Old-epoch readings reject even if their sequence is larger than the reset watermark.
runningTotal.resetOutput: Original reset with kind=totalReset, total=0.0, epoch, stateVersion, lastSequence, emittedAtMs, optional lastSampledAt.
runningTotal.recovery: All state is VOLATILE. Externally persist latest total/epoch/stateVersion/lastSequence/lastSampledAt checkpoint and the ordered input log, gate input on restart, and bootstrap/replay without duplicate downstream effects. Outputs provide checkpoint values, not an atomic durable transaction. Retained message/reset IDs are NOT restored; old sequences still reject but prior resetId reuse at a newer version cannot be recognized without the external durable log. No cross-restart exactly-once guarantee or autonomous persistence.

smoothReadings.decision: First observation initializes y1=x1. Every later accepted reading computes y=alpha*current value+(1-alpha)*previous smoothed output. It is per-reading exponential weighting, not a timed window or sample-count average; irregular sample timing does not alter alpha. Native-core ticks do nothing; the MQTT wrapper authorizes readings only and rejects ticks.
smoothReadings.output: Original reading with kind=smoothed, raw value unchanged, smoothedValue and emittedAtMs. No rounding. Finite arithmetic required; rejected duplicates/stale inputs/errors never update the previous output.

readingPatterns.qualification: All five fixtures run through Engine and the SDK Map/Filter wrapper; pure-core no-op smoothing ticks are explicitly rejected at the wrapper boundary. Local unit/fixture/WASI validation is not a real AIO deployment or publication claim. Main owns release stamping to a new immutable version, packaging integration, host timer research, and real-cluster qualification.

diagnostics.channel: Core/CLI returns kind=diagnostic records. SDK wrapper counts/logs them and replaces diagnostic-only results with pending. In mixed batches it removes diagnostics after logging, so operational records never become training samples.
diagnostics.graphFilter: A dedicated filter-only SDK component exports filter@1.1.0; the stateful component exports only map@1.1.0. This avoids AIO 1.6 selecting Map initialization for a filter node when a component exports both interfaces. The filter initializes without settings: true passes data and alignment batches; false drops pending, modelApplied and diagnostic records. Non-Message inputs, malformed JSON, non-object payloads and non-string kind fields are SDK errors. No filter rules or external MCR module are required.
diagnostics.metrics: Counters are incremented through the public SDK metrics API. Metric-export failures are not fatal to data processing. Diagnostic warning logs contain event identity and reason; schema errors produce error logs and SDK errors. Avoid sensitive IDs/payloads on sample topics.

restartAndScale.durability: All buffers, completed dedup, active models and update IDs are VOLATILE. SDK 1.1.3 exposes state-store get/set, but this example does not persist or atomically checkpoint state. No exactly-once or restart dedup guarantee.
restartAndScale.recovery: Before allowing readings after every restart, an external durable supervisor must provide the latest approved initialModels configuration (not stale demo v7), or gate readings while replaying an approved sequential model log from a known bootstrap. Replay active versions only in order. Persist model approval and update IDs outside WASM; MQTT delivery alone is not a durable activation transaction.
restartAndScale.correlatorRecovery: Pending and completed keys are lost on restart. If rebuilding from durable prediction/measurement logs, deduplicate downstream in an external durable sink using assetId+pieceId+runId; do not claim once-only output.
restartAndScale.scale: One runtime instance only; do not load-balance an asset across instances. This sample does not implement partition ownership, cross-instance locking, fitting, approval, or actuation.
restartAndScale.metadata: SDK Message transport metadata comes from the triggering arrival; input schema is cleared and content type is application/json. Buffered origin timestamps/IDs must live in JSON. A tick-triggered batch must not be interpreted as retaining each original input's MQTT metadata.

handoff.graphSchemaCaveat: The public 1.1.0 graph schema permits filter operations without a moduleConfigurations entry. It checks structure, not component exports, host registry-prefix resolution or successful AIO installation; those require separate qualification.
documentationChanges: Link the supplied sample instead of asking customers to invent custom artifacts.
Use full GHCR repository paths relative to the GHCR registry endpoint.
Add a tick to the aligner publish sequence and document batch envelopes.
Describe predictor persistence as external supervisor work, not volatile WASM durability.
Original prediction and measurement sampledAt values can conflict; use predictedAt/measuredAt or other disjoint fields.
handoff.publishingChanges: Publish six immutable artifacts: the map module, dedicated filter module, three graphs and Helm chart. Release stamping updates the two operation-specific module references to the same release version. All module IDs are repository paths relative to GHCR; the host prefixes every ID with that endpoint. Never replace the published rc.1 artifacts; the packaging fix targets 1.0.0-rc.2. Main owns publishing/version qualification and real-cluster verification; no deployment is claimed by this implementation.
